column2: On the authority of Abū Yaʿlā Shaddād ibn Aws (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said:

“Allah has prescribed excellence (iḥsān) in everything. So when you kill, kill well; and when you slaughter, slaughter well. Let each of you sharpen his blade and let him spare suffering to the animal he slaughters.” Reported by Muslim.

His words, “Allah has prescribed excellence in everything”: excellence is the opposite of doing ill, and “prescribed” means legislated and made obligatory. This is a religious prescription of the Sharīʿah, and the excellence it requires is general, for humans and animals alike.
Then the Messenger ﷺ commanded killing well and slaughtering well, sharpening the blade and sparing the slaughtered animal suffering.
This is one example of how excellence is shown when killing a person who deserves to be killed and when slaughtering an animal: by taking the easiest way of ending a life, without torment.
Ibn Rajab said in Jāmiʿ al-ʿUlūm wa-l-Ḥikam (1/381–382): “This hadith shows that excellence is obligatory in all deeds, but excellence in each thing is in keeping with what that thing is.

Excellence in performing the outward and inward obligations is performing them in a way that completes their obligatory parts; this degree of excellence in them is obligatory. As for excellence in them by completing their recommended parts, that is not obligatory.

Excellence in leaving the unlawful is refraining from it and leaving both its outward and its inward forms, as the Exalted said: ‘And leave the outward of sin and its inward’ [al-Anʿām 6:120]; this degree of excellence in it is obligatory. Excellence in patience with what is decreed

is to show patience with it properly, without resentment or panic. The obligatory excellence in dealing with people and living among them is to fulfil all the rights in this that Allah has made obligatory.

The obligatory excellence in having authority over people and governing them is fulfilling all the obligations of authority. What exceeds the obligatory in all of this is excellence that is not obligatory.

Excellence in killing those people and animals that may lawfully be killed is taking their life in the quickest, easiest and most expeditious way (awḥāhā, meaning the quickest), without adding to the torment, for that is pain for which there is no need.

This kind is the one the Prophet ﷺ mentioned in this hadith; perhaps he mentioned it as an example, or because there was a need to explain it in that situation. He said: ‘So when you kill, kill well (al-qitlah),

and when you slaughter, slaughter well (al-dhibḥah).’ Al-qitlah and al-dhibḥah, with an i (kasrah) after the first letter, denote the manner; the meaning is: make the manner of slaughtering and the manner of killing good. This shows that it is obligatory to be quick in taking those lives that may lawfully be taken, in the easiest way.”
Excellence in killing is required, without torture or mutilation, whether in fighting the disbelievers or in killing in retaliation or as a prescribed punishment,

except that when killing in retaliation, the killer is dealt with as he dealt with the one he killed, as is reported of the Prophet ﷺ when he had the Jew killed who had crushed a girl's head between two stones,

reported by al-Bukhārī (2413) and Muslim (1672), and as in the story of the men of ʿUraynah, reported by al-Bukhārī (6802) and Muslim (1671). As for the prescribed punishment of the married adulterer,
which is stoning, it is either an exception to the generality of this hadith, or it is understood that excellence lies in conforming to the Sharīʿah, and stoning the married adulterer is part of it.
Excellence is obligatory in everything.
Excellence is obligatory when killing, by taking the easiest way of taking life.
Excellence is likewise obligatory when slaughtering an animal.
One should check the instrument of slaughter before slaughtering,
because he ﷺ said: “Let each of you sharpen his blade and let him spare suffering to the animal he slaughters.”
